mainTopic: Who authored מסכת מדות? רב הונא says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the גמרא brings proofs, but רב אדא בר אהבה suggests the low eastern wall could follow רבי יהודה.
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא found that two sources disagree about the chambers of the בית המוקד. This amud finishes quoting that list from מסכת מדות. רב הונא then resolves the conflict: מדות was taught by רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who holds his own view. The first proof is a משנה about the four chambers of the עזרת נשים. In it, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says 'I forgot' what the fourth chamber was used for, which shows he is the one reporting the list. The גמרא then brings a second proof from the low eastern wall, which let the כהן burning the פרה אדומה on הר המשחה see the entrance of the היכל. Adding up all the steps shows that only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's extra step and דוכן make the entrance rise above the 20-אמה gate, so only his view explains why the wall had to be low. רב אדא בר אהבה rejects this proof. He says the low wall could instead follow רבי יהודה, who places the מזבח in the center of the עזרה. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The remaining chambers of the בית המוקד
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה from מדות finishes listing the corners of the בית המוקד: לחם הפנים, the hidden altar stones, and the way down to the immersion room.
steps.simpleTranslation: The southeast chamber was where they baked the לחם הפנים. In the northeast chamber the בית חשמונאי hid the altar stones that the gentile kings had defiled. From the northwest chamber they went down to the immersion room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from מסכת מדות that lists what each corner chamber of the בית המוקד was used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is the source that clashes with another משנה about the location of the lambs' chamber. The clash was raised on the previous amud. The rest of this passage explains why the two sources disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread placed weekly on the שולחן in the היכל
The Hasmonean family (the Chanukah heroes)
They stored away / hid permanently
Made them disgusting, i.e., defiled them with idol worship
The immersion room (מקוה) for the כהנים

phrases.english: The southeast one was the chamber
in which they would make the showbread.

phrases.aramaic: מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית — בָּהּ גָּנְזוּ בֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי
phrases.english: The northeast one: in it the Hasmoneans stored away
the altar stones that the gentile kings had defiled.
phrases.notes: Used for idol offerings, so they could no longer be used

phrases.aramaic: צְפוֹנִית מַעֲרָבִית — בָּהּ יוֹרְדִין לְבֵית הַטְּבִילָה.
phrases.english: The northwest one: through it they went down to the immersion room.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית הִיא לִשְׁכָּה שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote from מדות begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four corner chambers of the בית המוקד each had a set use, as listed in מדות.

steps.title: רב הונא: מסכת מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא resolves the conflict between the sources. מדות was taught by רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who holds his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Who taught מדות? It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction about where the lambs' chamber was. He says the two sources come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources do not need to agree, because מדות reflects the view of one תנא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The other משנה follows a different opinion. This turns a contradiction into a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?
מסכת מדות, the tractate describing the measurements of the מקדש
A תנא known for his precise knowledge of the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: A conflict between two משניות can be solved by saying each follows a different תנא. Here מדות = רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Who taught Middot?
It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאן תָּנָא מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised against the source just quoted
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a specific תנא (different authors)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both משניות speak for the same view, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who disagrees with the other source.

steps.title: The משנה about the chambers of the עזרת נשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from מדות about the עזרת נשים and its four corner chambers. This sets up the proof for רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The עזרת נשים was 135 אמות long by 135 wide. It had four chambers in its four corners. What were they used for? The southeast was the chamber of the נזירים, where they cooked their שלמים, shaved their hair, and threw it under the pot. The northeast was the woodshed, where blemished כהנים checked the logs for worms, because any wormy log is unfit for the מזבח. The northwest was the chamber of the מצורעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving רב הונא's claim by quoting a משנה in מדות. This part is setup; the key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three of the four chambers with no names attached. The proof depends on how the list ends with the fourth chamber. So the reader needs this whole list as background.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The women's courtyard of the מקדש
Its corners
People who took a vow of נזירות
כהנים with a physical blemish, unfit for the main עבודה
Checking for worms

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the chambers here with those in step 1. Step 1 was the בית המוקד; this משנה is about a different area, the עזרת נשים.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: עֶזְרַת נָשִׁים הָיְתָה אוֹרֶךְ מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ
phrases.english: The women's courtyard was 135 cubits long
by 135 cubits wide,
and there were four chambers in its four corners.
And what were they used for?

phrases.aramaic: דְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית — הִיא הָיְתָה לִשְׁכַּת הַנְּזִירִים,
phrases.english: The southeast one was the Chamber of the Nazirites,
for there the nazirites cook their peace-offerings
and shave their hair and throw it under the pot.
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in במדבר ו:יח.

phrases.aramaic: מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית — הִיא הָיְתָה לִשְׁכַּת דִּיר הָעֵצִים,
phrases.english: The northeast one was the Chamber of the Woodshed,
for there blemished priests stand
and check the logs for worms,
since any log that has a worm in it
is unfit for the altar.

phrases.aramaic: צְפוֹנִית מַעֲרָבִית — הִיא הָיְתָה לִשְׁכַּת הַמְצוֹרָעִין.
phrases.english: The northwest one was the Chamber of the Lepers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: עֶזְרַת נָשִׁים הָיְתָה אוֹרֶךְ מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רב הונא's attribution
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that מדות is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מדות listing the chambers of the עזרת נשים

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: I forgot the fourth chamber
steps.stepSummary: About the southwest chamber, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he forgot its use, and אבא שאול says it held wine and oil. This shows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the one reporting the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the southwest chamber, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said: I forgot what it was used for. אבא שאול says: They kept wine and oil there, and it was called 'the chamber of the house of oils.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the one telling us about the chambers, and he admits he forgot one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone says 'I forgot the fourth,' he must be the one who reported the first three. So the unnamed list in מדות comes from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. That supports רב הונא: מדות follows his view.

keyTerms.meaning: I forgot
A תנא who often records details of the מקדש
The chamber of the house of oils

steps.whatToRemember: The proof: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says 'I forgot' about one chamber. So he is the author of the whole list, and the anonymous voice of מדות is his.

phrases.english: As for the southwest one,
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov said:
I forgot what it was used for.
Abba Shaul says:
In it they would put wine and oil,
and it was called 'the Chamber of the House of Oils.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲרָבִית דְּרוֹמִית, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: שָׁכַחְתִּי מֶה הָיְתָה מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה and delivers the decisive proof
steps.raayaSupportSource: His own statement 'שכחתי' shows he is the narrator of the list

steps.title: Further support: the low eastern wall and the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that it is also reasonable that מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It quotes a משנה saying all the walls were high except the eastern one, so the כהן burning the פרה could see the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that this is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, as we learned: All the walls there were high, except the eastern wall. This was so the כהן burning the פרה, standing on הר המשחה, could aim and look toward the opening of the היכל while sprinkling the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second support for רב הונא. It quotes another משנה from מדות; the link to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is set up here and finished in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new source says the eastern wall was low so the כהן on הר המשחה could see the opening of the היכל. The גמרא will show that this detail matches a view held by רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. That would be a second sign that מדות is his.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, it is reasonable; introduces extra support
The eastern wall
The כהן who burns the פרה אדומה
The Mount of Olives, east of the מקדש
Sprinkling of the blood

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not yet the full proof. The גמרא has only quoted the source. Steps 6-8 collect the height measurements, and steps 9-11 link them to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable
that it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
as we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכְּתָלִים שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם הָיוּ גְּבוֹהִין,
phrases.english: All the walls that were there were high,
except for the eastern wall,
because the priest who burns the heifer
stands on the Mount of Olives

phrases.aramaic: וּמְכַוֵּון וְרוֹאֶה כְּנֶגֶד פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל
phrases.english: and aims and looks toward the entrance of the Sanctuary
at the time of sprinkling the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent support for רב הונא's attribution
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מדות about the low eastern wall for the פרה אדומה

steps.title: Gate height and the first set of steps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes משניות: every gate was 20 אמות high, then came the סורג, then the חיל with 12 steps of half an אמה each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: all the entrances there were twenty cubits high and ten cubits wide. And we learned: inside it was a lattice fence. And we learned: inside that was the חיל, ten cubits wide, and there were twelve steps there, each step half a cubit high and half a cubit deep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts collecting measurements from מדות so it can add up heights. This step is setting up a calculation that will pay off in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key number is the gate height: 20 אמות. Anything inside the מקדש that sits higher than 20 אמות above the eastern gate would be hidden from someone looking through it. The 12 steps of the חיל add 6 אמות of height.

keyTerms.meaning: Entrances / gates
A low lattice fence inside the הר הבית
A raised strip of ground (rampart) around the courtyards
Height
Its depth (how far each step goes in)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't lose track. The גמרא is not teaching architecture for its own sake. It is collecting numbers to add up the total height.

phrases.english: And we learned: all the entrances that were there
were twenty cubits high
and ten cubits wide.
And we learned: inside it was a lattice fence.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: לִפְנִים מִמֶּנּוּ הַחֵיל עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: And we learned: inside it was the rampart, ten cubits wide,
and there were twelve steps there,
each step half a cubit high
and half a cubit deep.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: כׇּל הַפְּתָחִים שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם גּוֹבְהָן עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the measurements needed to explain why the low eastern wall (step 5) was necessary.
steps.raayaObject: That מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: משניות in מדות about gate height and the steps of the חיל

steps.title: More steps up to the עזרת ישראל and the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: 15 steps lead from the עזרת נשים up to the עזרת ישראל, and 12 more steps are between the אולם and the מזבח, all half an אמה each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fifteen steps go up from inside it, going down from the עזרת ישראל to the עזרת נשים, each step half a cubit high and half a cubit deep. And we learned: between the אולם and the מזבח was twenty-two cubits, and there were twelve steps there, each half a cubit high and half a cubit deep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps adding measurements. It counts two more sets of steps on the way up to the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 15 steps add 7½ אמות, and the 12 steps near the אולם add 6 more. Running total so far: 6 + 7½ + 6 = 19½ אמות. That is still under the 20-אמה gate height.

keyTerms.meaning: The Women's Courtyard
The Israelites' Courtyard
The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The altar

phrases.english: Fifteen steps go up from within it,
going down from the Israelites' Courtyard to the Women's Courtyard,
each step half a cubit high
and half a cubit deep.
And we learned: between the Entrance Hall and the altar
was twenty-two cubits,
and there were twelve steps there,
each step half a cubit high
and half a cubit deep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the height calculation begun in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: משניות in מדות about the steps to the עזרת ישראל and between the אולם and מזבח

steps.title: The extra step and platform of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds a one-אמה step with the דוכן on it, which has three more half-אמה steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: there was a step there one cubit high, and the platform was placed on it, and it had three steps of half a cubit each.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the one opinion that adds extra height. These are the numbers that will push the total over 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds 1 אמה for the step plus 1½ אמות for the דוכן's three steps. That adds 2½ אמות, so the new total is 19½ + 2½ = 22 אמות. Now the entrance of the היכל is higher than the 20-אמה gate.

keyTerms.meaning: A step
The platform where the לוים stood and sang

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And we learned: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
there was a step there, one cubit high,
and the platform was placed on it,
and on it were three steps
of half a cubit each.
phrases.notes: That adds 1 + 1½ = 2½ אמות more, bringing the total to 22 אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: מַעֲלָה הָיְתָה שָׁם וּגְבוֹהָ אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final measurements, which only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds.
steps.raayaObject: That מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in מדות about the extra step and the דוכן

steps.title: Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב explains why the entrance was hidden
steps.stepSummary: If מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the היכל entrance (22 אמות up) is hidden by the 20-אמה gate. That explains why the eastern wall had to be low.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, that is why the entrance was hidden from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the math and draws the point. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the view of the היכל would be blocked, so the low eastern wall makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With his extra steps, the היכל entrance sits 22 אמות up, higher than the 20-אמה gate. So the כהן on הר הזיתים could not see it through the gate, which is why the eastern wall was built low (step 5). Without those extra steps the total is only 19½, so the low wall would not be needed. This supports רב הונא that מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well if you say…
That is why / this explains
Was hidden / covered
The entrance (of the היכל)

steps.whatToRemember: Gate = 20 אמות. Steps without רבי אליעזר בן יעקב = 19½. With him = 22. Only at 22 is the היכל hidden, which explains the low eastern wall. So מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.confusionAlert: The word בשלמא means this works well according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and it signals a contrast to come. The next step states the contrast outright: according to the רבנן there would be no reason for the low wall.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
that is why the entrance was hidden from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the total from steps 6-8 to explain the low eastern wall from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The height calculation: 22 אמות exceeds the 20-אמה gate only according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: Under the רבנן, half an אמה of the entrance would still show
steps.stepSummary: If מדות followed the רבנן, the low eastern wall would not be needed, because half an אמה of the היכל entrance would already be visible through the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say it follows the רבנן, there is half an אמה through which he can see the entrance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the other side of the calculation. Without רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's extra steps, the כהן would already see part of the entrance through the gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra 2.5 אמות, the steps add up to 6 + 7.5 + 6 = 19.5 אמות. The gate is 20 אמות high, so the bottom half אמה of the היכל entrance would be visible through it. If that is enough, there would be no reason to make the eastern wall low.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view), who do not count רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's extra step and דוכן
Half an אמה
The entrance (of the היכל)
Is visible / can be seen

steps.confusionAlert: The half אמה does not come from the walls. It is the gap between the gate's height (20) and the height of the היכל entrance (19.5) under the רבנן.

phrases.english: But if you say it follows the Rabbis,
there is half an amah
through which the entrance is visible to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun in Step 9 by showing that the רבנן's numbers do not fit the low eastern wall.
steps.raayaObject: That מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The height calculation: under the רבנן the view through the gate is not blocked, so the low eastern wall would be pointless.

steps.title: So it must be רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws its conclusion: מדות must follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not conclude from this that it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof. Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's numbers explain why the eastern wall had to be low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the gate blocks the view of the entrance, so the wall had to be lowered. Under the רבנן, nothing blocks the view. So the low wall seems to show that מדות is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not to be learned from this? (a formula that closes a proof)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to be concluded from this
that it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion of the proof built in Steps 5 to 10.
steps.raayaObject: מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The low eastern wall fits only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's step heights.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: it could be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rejects the proof and says the low eastern wall can follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה pushes back on the proof. He says there is another תנא whose view also explains the low eastern wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the only possible explanation. רב אדא בר אהבה offers a second explanation, רבי יהודה, so the proof is no longer decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who challenges the proof
Whose view is this? (introduces an alternative attribution)
A תנא offered as the source of the low-wall view

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of Step 11 by offering a different תנא as the source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the low eastern wall proves מדות follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed no other view explains the low wall, but רבי יהודה's view can also explain it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the מזבח stood in the center and was 32 אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה's source: a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says the מזבח was centered in the עזרה and measured 32 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says the מזבח is centered and stands in the middle of the עזרה, and it was 32 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that backs up רב אדא בר אהבה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain how this placement of the מזבח led to the low eastern wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה places the מזבח right in the middle of the עזרה, lined up with the entrances. Because of where it stands and how big it is, it can block the view toward the היכל entrance. That gives a reason for the low wall that does not depend on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's extra steps.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
The altar
Centered
The Temple courtyard

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The altar is centered and stands
in the middle of the courtyard,
phrases.notes: Lined up with the entrances of the courtyards and the היכל

phrases.english: and it was thirty-two amos,
phrases.notes: 32 by 32 אמות; the ברייתא continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא supporting רב אדא בר אהבה's claim in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the low eastern wall can follow רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה describes the מזבח as centered in the עזרה and 32 אמות in size.
